newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa prepares law for Telkom privatisation.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa prepares law for Telkom privatisation.

text.p: The South African government on Thursday tabled legislation to make it possible for the state-owned Telkom telecommunications corporation to sell 30 percent of its equity to a foreign consortium in April.

The Posts, Telecommunications and Broadcasting Ministry announced on Monday that SBC Communications Inc and Telekom Malaysia Bhd would enter final negotiations as a consortium for a 30 percent stake in the concern.
Analysts say the stake could fetch some six billion rand.
But the deal cannot be finalised until parliament has adopted the Post Office Amendment Bill tabled in Cape Town on Thursday.
The amendment seeks to cancel a statutory prohibition on the sale of Telkom equity to more than one shareholder and to anyone other than the state.

"When Telkom acquires a strategic equity partner, certain amendments to the Post Office Act will have to be effected to enable Telkom to operate as the same company, but with more than one shareholder," the ministry said in a memorandum supporting theproposed amendment.
The amendment also provides an alternative channel for state subsidies to the loss-making postal service, which currently is supported by Telkom.

The bill proposes that for the next five years, parliament should be empowered to vote state funds for the operation of the postal service, which the government has vowed to make profitable within that time.

A second bill tabled on Thursday provides for the transfer of staff from the existing Department of Communications to the new and independent South African Telecommunications Regulatory Authority, which will oversee the country's privatised communicatons industry.
"The skills to perform these highly technical and other functions have been accumulated over many years and are not freely available on the open market," the ministry said.
Necessary staff should be asked to transfer to the new regulatory authority with full continuation of their service, pension, holiday and other benefits, the bill proposes.
